# Orchestrator-Topology Golden Baseline

Frozen renders of `rules/1-generic/a2a-delegation-gates.md` for the two
required AC-6/AC-18 states. Both projects leave `orchestrator.topology`
**unset**; only the orchestrator role state differs:

| Fixture | Role state | Rendered gate |
|---|---|---|
| `a2a-delegation-gates.role-inactive.md` | `ROLE_ORCHESTRATOR_ACTIVE=false` | `Worker → HARD REJECT` |
| `a2a-delegation-gates.role-active.md` | `ROLE_ORCHESTRATOR_ACTIVE=true` | ``Worker → `orchestrator` → HARD REJECT`` |

The pair differs by exactly the `` → `orchestrator` `` fragment. That is the
regression guard for AC-6: an unset topology key must keep today's bytes in
both role states, including the fail-closed `ORCH_TOPOLOGY_EXPLICIT` else
branch. A drift here is a real regression, **not** a rebaseline candidate.

## Declared vs derived `subagent` (issue #1190, AC-36)

Two further fixtures pin the OTHER half of the same conditional — that the
branch is chosen by `ORCH_TOPOLOGY_EFFECTIVE_EXPLICIT`, not by the effective
value alone (both states are `effective == subagent`):

| Fixture | `orchestrator.topology` | Rendered gate 2 |
|---|---|---|
| `a2a-delegation-gates.declared-subagent.md` | `subagent` (`source: project`) | `Orchestrator-Topologie (subagent)` branch |
| `a2a-delegation-gates.derived-subagent.md` | unset, derived `subagent` | `Orchestrator-Singleton` branch |

Outside gate 2 the two renders are byte-identical. The derived fixture is the
same bytes as `a2a-delegation-gates.role-active.md` (declaring nothing must not
move the render). Both are generated by
`tests/test_opencode_positions.py::_render_gate_rule` through the real sync —
never hand-written.

## How the fixtures were generated

Through the real sync path, never hand-written. `tests/test_ac01_render_identity.py`
exposes the generator (`render_topology_rule`); it synced a scratch project
(provider `Claude`, `dod-preset: rapid-prototyping`) into
`<scratch>/.claude/rules/a2a-delegation-gates.md` and copied the normalised
bytes:

```bash
python3 - <<'PY'
import sys, tempfile
from pathlib import Path
sys.path.insert(0, "tests")
import test_ac01_render_identity as h

out = Path("tests/fixtures/topology-golden")
with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as td:
    for role_active, name in (
        (False, h._TOPOLOGY_GOLDEN_INACTIVE),
        (True, h._TOPOLOGY_GOLDEN_ACTIVE),
    ):
        text = h.render_topology_rule(role_active, Path(td) / str(role_active))
        (out / name).write_bytes(text.encode("utf-8"))
PY
```

The **role state** is expressed through the project's `roles:` allowlist
(ActiveSet): the inactive project lists `developer`, `documenter`,
`security-auditor`, `code-reviewer`, the active project omits the key (every
gate-enabled role stays active). Keeping the two security-critical roles in the
inactive whitelist makes the role gate the *only* byte difference between the
two fixtures.

## Normalisation

Same discipline as the AC-01 harness (`_hash_file`):

- CRLF folded to LF;
- volatile scratch roots replaced with `<ROOT>`;
- `model:` lines pinned to `model: <MODEL>`.

The rule render contains no model line, no root and no date today, so the
normalisation is a no-op that keeps the contract explicit.

Frozen after Task 15 of `docs/plans/2026-11-04-orchestrator-topology-v1-plan.md`.
The Task 18 rule amendment (conditional topology branch) must leave these bytes
unchanged when the key is unset; `test_topology_golden_key_unset_is_byte_identical`
is the guard. Do not regenerate without a documented AC-6 reason.

## Orchestrator end-state goldens (issue #1190, AC-16/AC-17/AC-26/AC-27/AC-36)

The five `orchestrator.*` fixtures plus `schema-property-paths.json` freeze the
Task 21 end state of the mode-topology gate. Every `.md` fixture is a FULL
`agents/1-generic/orchestrator.md` render through the real per-role sync path
(`tests/test_orchestrator_topology_effective_flags.py::render_orchestrator`) —
never hand-written.

| Fixture | Provider | Project state | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| `orchestrator.unset-derived-subagent.claude.md` | Claude | `topology` unset, `orchestrator` NOT in the ActiveSet | frozen `aaed14c2` template replayed with the CURRENT renderer (AC-16/AC-27 baseline) |
| `orchestrator.unset-derived-subagent.opencode.md` | Opencode | same | same baseline for Opencode |
| `orchestrator.unset-derived-subagent.gemini.md` | Gemini | same | same baseline for Gemini |
| `orchestrator.derived-primary.opencode.md` | Opencode | `topology` unset, `orchestrator` in the ActiveSet (Opencode declares `primary-role: orchestrator`) | intentional AC-17 primary branch |
| `orchestrator.declared-primary.md` | Claude | `orchestrator.topology: primary` | AC-27 declared primary branch |
| `orchestrator.declared-subagent.md` | Claude | `orchestrator.topology: subagent` | AC-36 explicit branch |

The three `unset-derived-subagent.*` files are generated from
`git show aaed14c2:agents/1-generic/orchestrator.md` through
`render_orchestrator(provider, ..., template_text=baseline)`. The test
`test_unset_topology_subagent_render_is_byte_identical` asserts that the
working-tree template renders the same BODY in that state and that only
`version:` and `generated-from:` move (the two release pins).

`schema-property-paths.json` freezes the recursive `properties` path set of
`config/project-config.schema.json` at `a41745e` (pre-implementation, 331
paths). `test_schema_has_no_new_properties` fails on any added or removed
property; `description`/`title`/`enum` values are explicitly out of scope
(AC-26).

Regenerate the `.md` goldens only with the helper above (a documented reason
belongs in the test module's docstring). Do not hand-edit them.
